title: Topology-Aware Neural Collapse for Generalized Category Discovery on Graphs

problem.claim: Graph GCD requires representations that recognize known categories and discover novel categories from limited labeled data.

gap.claim: Topology-induced neighborhood smoothing conflicts with the strict Simplex ETF convergence required by neural collapse.

contributions.claim: TopoNC is a topology-aware neural collapse framework for Graph GCD.
TopoNC fixes Simplex ETF prototypes as global geometric targets and uses a gated Dual-Stream Encoder to separate topology smoothing from feature-discriminative learning.
TopoNC uses Topology-Conditioned Pseudo-Labeling with Sinkhorn-based global balancing, Old-Class Top-K Admission Masking, and Neighborhood-Consensus Screening.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets.
The authors report that TopoNC consistently outperforms existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph GCD needs stable and discriminative representations for recognizing known and discovering novel categories with limited labels.
Neural Collapse uses maximally separated class representations aligned with Simplex ETF prototypes.
Graph topology induces local smoothing that conflicts with Simplex ETF convergence.
TopoNC combines fixed Simplex ETF targets, a gated Dual-Stream Encoder, and topology-conditioned pseudo-labeling.
The authors report consistent improvements over existing methods on several benchmark datasets.

unknowns: No benchmark dataset names, baselines, metrics, or numerical results are provided.
No implementation, training details, ablations, or computational-cost information is provided.
The abstract does not quantify the effect of individual TopoNC components.
